en.title: Inactive Skills in a Closed Request Window
en.description:
Each log entry is a skillId and a timestamp. For each query q, count the skills that have no request in the closed interval [q−timeWindow,q]; output the answers in the input order of the queries.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O and judging; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains numSkills m q timeWindow, all four in 1..100000; then m lines of skill timestamp, then one line of q queryTime values. skill is in 1..numSkills, and all times are in 1..100000.
en.output: One line of q inactive counts, separated by spaces.
en.explanation: Example 1: for q=3 the window [1,3] contains skills 1 and 2, so 1 skill is inactive; for q=4 the window [2,4] contains only skill 2, so 2 are inactive. Example 2: query 5 has skill 1, so 1 is inactive; query 1 has no logs, so 2 are inactive, and the original order is kept. Example 3: both log entries belong to skill 1, which counts as only one active skill, so 0 are inactive.
hints: Sort the logs by time, and sort the queries too while keeping their original indices. With two pointers, add logs with time ≤q and remove logs with time <q−window, maintaining the active count with per-skill frequencies.
